newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. rice group to launch sales campaign in Japan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rice group to launch sales campaign in Japan.

text.p: The U.S. Rice Federation said on Tuesday it will launch a campaign to promote sales of American rice in Japan, spending about $450,000 through May.
Under the plan, the rice industry body said it will ask some large supermarket and convenience store chains to promote U.S. rice to its customers.
Lower-than-expected sales of foreign rice in Japanese market motivated the U.S. industry body to launch the promotional campaign, its senior official said.
"We would hoped originally there would be better acceptance of U.S. rice here," William Farmer, regional director of the U.S. rice industry body, told reporters in Tokyo.
"But it became evident that much different strategy is required," he said, adding that the U.S. Rice Federation has opened a Japan office.

Under the GATT Uruguay Round accords in 1993, Japan agreed to open its long-closed rice market and to increase annual import quotas gradually. It bought 511,000 tonnes, including brown and milled rice, in the 1996/97 fiscal year ending this March.
